evolution_chain.description: Civil Rights Act of 1871 §1 (KKK Act) — original enactment
Revised Statutes §1979 — first codification; adds 'and laws' to scope, adds Territory, restructures
Monroe v. Pape — doctrinal revival after 90-year dormancy (case law, not textual amendment)
Pub. L. 96-170 — DC extension (adds 'or the District of Columbia')
Pub. L. 104-317 §309(c) — judicial immunity (bars injunctive relief against judges in judicial capacity). LAST TEXTUAL AMENDMENT.
Pointer to current/ — text unchanged since 1996

case_law_documented.role: interpretive — the revival; 'under color of' means misuse of state-given authority

case_law_documented.case: Monell v. Dept of Social Services
case_law_documented.role: interpretive — municipalities are 'persons' under §1983 but liable only for policy/custom
uphold — established qualified immunity defense for police officers under §1983
interpretive — reformulated qualified immunity from subjective good faith to objective 'clearly established law' test
interpretive — eliminated mandatory Saucier sequencing; courts can skip merits and grant QI on 'clearly established' alone
strike — 'obvious clarity' exception; some conduct so egregious that QI fails without factually identical precedent
interpretive — 'and laws' means ALL federal statutes, not just civil rights laws; the 1874 recodification's two-word expansion realized 106 years later
interpretive — QI specificity requirement; 'clearly established' must match the specific factual context, not just the general right
interpretive — judicial immunity does not bar injunctive relief (later overridden by 1996 amendment §309(c))
